content.text: I have enough to assess. The termination article contains a full exit/transition package in our favor.

input.quote: 14.3.2 effective as of such termination, SFJ shall, and it hereby does, assign to PB all of SFJ's and its Affiliates' right, title and interest in and to all Product Filings then owned or Controlled by SFJ or any of its Affiliates; provided that if any such Product Filing is not immediately transferable in a country, SFJ shall provide PB with all benefit of such Product Filing and such assistance and cooperation as necessary or reasonably requested by PB to timely transfer such Product Filing to PB or its designee
input.rationale: The agreement already delivers, in our favor, everything this rule targets and more. On any termination, § 14.3 (p0782–p0789) requires SFJ to (i) assign sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package and Research Results to PB (§ 14.3.1, and § 11.1.1.4 buy-back), (ii) assign all Product Filings and, where a filing is not immediately transferable, give PB the full benefit plus "such assistance and cooperation as necessary or reasonably requested by PB" (§ 14.3.2), (iii) within a set period deliver true, correct and complete copies of all Product Filings and disclose all previously-undisclosed Research Results (§ 14.3.3), (iv) at PB's sole election either wind down the Clinical Trials at SFJ's cost or transfer control to PB and continue conducting them for a stated period to enable transfer without interruption (§ 14.3.4), and (v) assign all CRO, Site and Vendor Agreements and cooperate on transition notices (§ 14.3.5). Deletion/return of our confidential materials is covered by § 10.3, which gives the disclosing party the choice of return or destruction "with such destruction being certified in writing by an authorized officer of the Receiving Party." These provisions are at or above the preferred position: data/records come back to us, transition assistance is available at PB's election (trial continuation at PB's cost, mirroring the "then-current rates" concept), and certified destruction follows. The specific day/month periods are redacted as "[***]" in this copy and the assistance duration is not expressed as a flat six months — we should confirm the redacted periods on the execution copy, but these are timing details rather than material failures, and § 14.4.3 expressly makes Articles 10 and 11 and §§ 14.2–14.3 survive termination. No redline warranted; this is a customer-favorable exit regime.
